stop_rules: STOP if exact CPython 3.11.9 64-bit is unavailable or if the py launcher resolves a different interpreter.
STOP if the materialization root already exists; do not delete, repair, merge, or reuse it without a new control decision.
STOP on any frozen source path, size, or SHA-256 mismatch, or if the candidate/revision/tree identity differs.
STOP if any network host outside the allowlist appears in pip logs, including an unapproved mirror, VCS host, or package index.
STOP if any third-party dependency lacks a compatible wheel, if pip proposes an sdist/egg, or if a wheel tag is incompatible with CPython 3.11 Windows AMD64.
STOP if torch does not resolve to exactly 2.2.2+cpu from the official CPU index or if a CUDA/ROCm/nvidia/triton distribution appears.
STOP on duplicate normalized package identities, direct-pin substitution, resolver conflict, hash mismatch, or non-deterministic second resolution.
STOP if the legacy local wheel build accesses the network, mutates the frozen source, produces zero or multiple wheels, or emits metadata other than RecBole 1.2.1.
STOP if pip check is non-zero, any exact version assertion fails, any bounded import fails, torch reports a CUDA build/device, or syntax compilation fails.
STOP if any command contains or invokes a forbidden training, evaluation, tuning, checkpoint, download, or project TEST operation.
STOP when any timeout, byte limit, process limit, or expected-write-set boundary is exceeded.
STOP rather than changing Python, torch, NumPy, Ray, any direct pin, the source revision, the source code, or the feature exclusions. Escalate to a new reviewed proposal.
